hypothesis: COG3017 (outer membrane lipoprotein involved in outer membrane biogenesis; LptE/RlpB-type, LPS assembly at the Gram-negative outer membrane) is increased/characteristic in 5-month-old infants relative to 12-month-old infants.
rationale: No study was found that reports COG3017 (or its named homolog LptE/RlpB) itself as differentially abundant between ~5-month and ~12-month infant gut metagenomes; searches for the COG ID and gene names returned only bacteriological/structural literature (LptE as the outer-membrane lipoprotein partner of LptD in the Lpt LPS-transport machine), with no infant-cohort context. Support for the hypothesis is therefore pathway- and taxon-level and indirect: a human infant metagenomic study of the complementary feeding transition (stool at 4, 9 and 12 months) reported that sequences assigned to 'biosynthesis of lipopolysaccharides' decreased in relative abundance over time, and multiple infant cohorts report that Escherichia/Enterobacteriaceae (LPS-rich Gram-negatives that carry lptE) peak in early infancy and decline by 12 months. However, the same age window is characterised by a rapid expansion of Bacteroides/Bacteroidaceae (also Gram-negative, also encoding LptE-family outer-membrane lipoproteins) between 4 and 12 months, so the total Gram-negative outer-membrane gene pool need not fall with age; some cohorts even find Bacteroidetes-dominant communities at 12 months. Because the directly relevant evidence is generic/pathway-level and the taxonomic reasoning is internally conflicting, this scores 1 (weak/mixed), not 2.

evidence.title: Adaptation of the infant gut microbiome during the complementary feeding transition
evidence.study_population: Healthy human infants sampled at three 'snapshot' timepoints (approximately 4, 9 and 12 months) across the complementary feeding period; shotgun metagenomic functional profiling plus metabolites
evidence.relevance: Direct human-infant, age-matched functional evidence in the hypothesised direction at pathway level: sequences assigned to 'biosynthesis of lipopolysaccharides' and associated protein-family pathways decreased in relative abundance with increasing age, implying a larger Gram-negative envelope/LPS gene pool earlier in infancy. It does not test COG3017/LptE (LPS transport/OM assembly) specifically.

evidence.title: Effect of Environmental Exposures on the Gut Microbiota from Early Infancy to Two Years of Age
evidence.study_population: Human infants followed longitudinally from 1 month to 2 years (16S rRNA profiling, LonGP trajectory models)
evidence.relevance: Indirect taxonomic support and partial contradiction: Escherichia declined as the microbiota matured over the first year (favouring higher Enterobacteriaceae-derived outer-membrane genes at ~5 months), while Bacteroides increased rapidly after 6 months (Bacteroides also encodes LptE-family outer-membrane lipoproteins, which could offset or reverse the expected COG3017 trend by 12 months).

evidence.title: Bacterial Gut Microbiota and Infections During Early Childhood
evidence.study_population: Review summarising a large Swedish birth cohort (Roswall et al. 2021) with 16S profiling at newborn, 4 months, 12 months, 3 and 5 years
evidence.relevance: Corroborates the compositional context for both directions: Enterobacteriaceae (with Bifidobacterium, Enterococcus, Streptococcus, Lactobacillus) peak at 4 months, whereas Bacteroides increases rapidly between 4 and 12 months — i.e. Gram-negative outer-membrane gene carriers shift in identity rather than uniformly declining.

evidence.title: Age-associated gut microbiome succession, colonization resistance, and relative resistome patterns in an antibiotic-restricted infant cohort
evidence.study_population: 82 shotgun metagenomes from 54 healthy human infants (1 month and 6 months of age)
evidence.relevance: Indirect support: Enterobacteriaceae relative abundance fell sharply with age within early infancy (median 16.6% at 1 month vs 1.9% at 6 months), consistent with declining LPS/outer-membrane-biogenesis gene carriage as infants age — but the comparison stops at 6 months and does not extend to 12 months.

evidence.title: Lipoprotein LptE is required for the assembly of LptD by the beta-barrel assembly machine in the outer membrane of Escherichia coli
evidence.study_population: Escherichia coli laboratory genetics/biochemistry (not a human study)
evidence.relevance: Establishes the functional identity behind COG3017: LptE is an essential outer-membrane lipoprotein of the LptD/E complex required for LPS insertion into the outer leaflet, so the COG is expected to track Gram-negative (LPS-producing) taxa abundance. Used only to justify the taxonomic proxy reasoning, not as evidence about infant age.

contradicting_evidence: The strongest counterweight is that Bacteroides/Bacteroidaceae — Gram-negative organisms that also encode LptE-family outer-membrane lipoproteins and LPS — expand rapidly between 4 and 12 months in multiple infant cohorts (Roswall-based summary; Microorganisms 2021 trajectory models; a 1-year Italian cohort noting Bacteroidaceae rise with cessation of milk feeding), and Bacteroidetes-dominant clusters are common at 12 months. Thus even though Enterobacteriaceae/Escherichia fall with age, total outer-membrane-biogenesis gene abundance at 12 months could equal or exceed that at 5 months. No study was found directly reporting COG3017 higher at ~5 vs ~12 months, so this is unresolved rather than a clean contradiction.

caveats: COG3017 is a broadly distributed housekeeping gene present in essentially all Gram-negative gut bacteria, so its metagenomic abundance is largely a proxy for the aggregate Gram-negative fraction rather than a specific biological signal; direction therefore depends on the relative balance of Proteobacteria (declining) versus Bacteroidetes (rising) in the particular cohort, which varies with feeding mode, delivery mode, geography and antibiotic exposure. Relative-abundance gene profiles are also compositional, so a decline can reflect expansion of Gram-positive Firmicutes rather than an absolute drop. No literature was found addressing this exact COG at these exact timepoints; the PLOS One evidence concerns LPS biosynthesis rather than the Lpt outer-membrane assembly module.
